:::{#exm-no-real-imaginary-unit}
#### No real number squares to $-1$

The imaginary unit is not a real number,
because the square of every real number $x$ is at least $0$:

- if $x \ge 0$, then $x^2 = x \cd x$ is a product of two nonnegative numbers, so $x^2 \ge 0$;
- if $x < 0$, then $x^2 = x \cd x$ is a product of two negative numbers, so $x^2 > 0$.

For instance, $3^2 = 9$ and $(-3)^2 = 9$;
neither is $-1$.
So the equation $x^2 = -1$ has no real solution,
and @def-imaginary-unit introduces a new number to solve it.

:::
